title: Jermaine Thomas, Born on US Army Base in Germany, Deported to Jamaica He'd Never Visited
description_short: Jermaine Thomas, Born on US Army Base in Germany, Deported to Jamaica He'd Never Visited
description_medium: Yahoo’s fact-check confirms that Jermaine Thomas was deported to Jamaica in May 2025 after an immigration judge’s 2013 removal order and a federal appeals court ruling that he was not a U.S. citizen. Thomas was born at a U.S. military base in Germany and had not previously visited Jamaica. The linked account distinguishes those facts from the broader claim that his deportation was unlawful.
description_long: A Yahoo fact check confirmed that Jermaine Thomas was deported to Jamaica in May 2025 after immigration authorities carried out a final removal order. Thomas, the son of a U.S. Army veteran, was born at a U.S. military base in Germany and spent most of his life in Texas. He argued that his birth circumstances entitled him to U.S. citizenship, but a federal appeals court ruled that he was not a citizen and could be removed. ICE told the fact-checking outlet that an immigration judge had ordered his removal in December 2013, and the Department of Homeland Security said he had final removal orders. The report also notes convictions including drug possession, driving while intoxicated, assault, theft and robbery. The case drew attention because Thomas was sent to Jamaica, which he said he had never visited. These facts distinguish the verified deportation from broader claims about his citizenship or the legal history behind it. The linked report does not establish that he was stateless or that the removal rested solely on his birthplace.

notes: Corrected the earlier long description to match the linked Yahoo fact check, which identifies a federal appeals court ruling and an immigration judge’s 2013 removal order, rather than a Supreme Court ruling.

title: NOAA Gutted: 2,000+ Climate and Weather Scientists Fired
description_short: NOAA Gutted: 2,000+ Climate and Weather Scientists Fired
description_medium: The supplied account says NOAA lost about 2,000 employees—roughly a quarter of its workforce—after layoffs began in February 2025, including more than 800 staff in one day. It also describes proposed cuts to oceanic and atmospheric research. Scientists warned that reducing staff could weaken hurricane, wildfire-weather and climate monitoring; the record does not document the eventual effect on forecasts.
description_long: The supplied account says the Trump administration began large-scale layoffs at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration in February 2025. More than 800 employees were reportedly dismissed on February 27, with additional reductions planned; by March, the agency had lost about 2,000 staff, roughly one quarter of its workforce since January. The White House budget office also proposed eliminating NOAA’s Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research and reducing the agency’s budget from $6.1 billion to $4.5 billion. Scientists warned that losing staff and research capacity could weaken hurricane forecasting, wildfire-weather prediction and climate monitoring as climate-related hazards intensified. The BBC source is linked for this account, but the supplied record does not include the final budget decision, the agency’s revised staffing total, or a measured change in forecast performance. The documented issue is therefore the scale of the staffing and budget proposals and the risks raised by researchers, not proof that a particular forecast failed because of the cuts.

preserved_fields.title: NOAA Gutted: 2,000+ Climate and Weather Scientists Fired
preserved_fields.description_short: NOAA Gutted: 2,000+ Climate and Weather Scientists Fired

notes: needs_context: The linked BBC article reports about 880 NOAA employees, including weather forecasters, fired in one day in February 2025. It does not establish the title’s cumulative 2,000-plus climate and weather scientist figure or document the later staffing total. Provide a dated agency staffing count and a source establishing the cumulative losses before treating that figure as verified.
